newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap-Gas oil rises after Friday's dip.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap-Gas oil rises after Friday's dip.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps saw further gains on Monday, tracking a supportive crude market with most brokers and traders assessing the market's upward momentum still intact.
August swaps were last quoted at $22.90/$23.20 and September at $23.50/$23.60, up from last Friday's quotes at $22.75/$22.85 and $23.10/$23.25 respectively.
Brokers attributed the rise to a supportive crude market.
Brent for September was last quoted at $18.53/$18.70 per barrel, up from the London's IPE settlement of $18.53 after a gain of nine cents.
NYMEX September crude rose 12 cents to $19.89 in New York, boosted by a tightening gasoline market.

"Swaps levels are likely to move higher, borrowing strength from crude market despite the slight dip seen in the cash market on Friday. The downtrend are not likely to start today, maybe later this week as Chinese demand are very thin," said one trader.

In the cash market, traders were divided between the bulls and bears. Some traders said the cash market is still bullish with the recent spate of strong buying interests by traders who were primarily covering their short-positions into Indonesia.
A handful of traders have in total purchased over 1.1 million barrels in the first four days of last week.
While prices had lost some grounds late Friday, brokers projected the dip to be temporary and expected levels to continue their upward climb later Monday.
Gas oil values edged down by about 10 cents in the physical market on Friday as buyers moved to the sidelines while an aggressive major emerge to get rid of some of its physical cargoes.
But some traders said Friday's dip could be a start of a downtrend.
They cited poor demand from China and high stocks seen both at the mainland and Singapore and an overhang seen in the prompt market.
Singapore middle distillate stocks for the week ending July 23 rose by 469,000 barrels to 11.084 million, the Trade Development Board said on Thursday.
